response:
Repairing the prior failure: the validator requires at least one variable exclusive to each theme. The only quality-exclusive variables are revt, cogs, dp; the only distress-exclusive ones are pi, txt, che, wcap. Every proposal below contains at least one from each exclusive set, and I rebuild the mechanisms around what those variables genuinely measure (cost structure / margin quality / capital consumption vs. liquidity buffer, pretax loss state, working-capital slack).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: LossGatedGrossProfitCoverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(NEG(pi), 0), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), lt)))
HYPOTHESIS: Among firms currently reporting a pretax loss (the distress state), the ones whose gross profit still covers a large fraction of total liabilities have a viable operating core and recover, while loss-makers whose gross profit is small relative to obligations face restructuring; for profitable firms this coverage difference carries little default information.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The pretax-loss indicator switches the signal on only in the distressed state and leaves healthy firms at the neutral value zero, so the predictive content is genuinely state-dependent rather than an unconditional gross-profitability effect. Gross profit (revt minus cogs) is the most persistent quality flow available and is unpolluted by the write-offs and one-off charges that drive reported losses.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: MarginDecayXCashDrain
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(cogs, revt), 5)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Distress is a process, not a level: firms whose cost-of-sales ratio has been trending up for years (eroding gross margin quality) and which are simultaneously drawing down their cash buffer are on a depletion path that the market prices with a lag, producing low subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Neither a slow margin slide nor a single year of cash decline is alarming alone; jointly they indicate that internal funds are shrinking exactly as unit economics deteriorate. Using a 5-year trend for the quality channel and a one-year change for the liquidity channel matches the different speeds at which operating deterioration and financing stress manifest.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: MarginStabilityXPretaxDebtCoverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(pi, lt)), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Pretax earnings coverage of total liabilities is a much more reliable solvency measure when the underlying gross margin is stable; firms with strong coverage and stable margins are safe and richly rewarded, while weak coverage combined with volatile margins marks unpriced default risk.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Gross-margin volatility is the quality dimension that determines how much information a single year's coverage ratio contains, so multiplying the two ranks sharpens the distress ordering instead of restating it. Pretax income (pi) is used rather than net income to avoid tax and special-item noise in the coverage channel.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: NegativeWorkingCapitalProfitSort
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(NEG(wcap), 0), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Negative working capital is ambiguous: for profitable firms it reflects efficient supplier financing and fast inventory turns, but for weakly profitable firms it is a liquidity shortfall. Sorting the negative-working-capital subsample on gross profitability should therefore generate a large spread, with efficient operators outperforming genuinely illiquid firms.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This tests a sign-interpretation flip rather than a monotone composite: the same balance-sheet configuration means opposite things depending on operating quality, which no single-theme signal can express. Firms with positive working capital are held at neutral zero so the spread is driven entirely by the conditioned subsample.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: CapitalConsumptionAdjustedLiquidity
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, lt)))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating cash flow flatters firms whose cash flow is mostly the depreciation add-back; subtracting dp isolates cash earnings net of capital consumption, and this true cash-generating capacity is what makes a given cash-to-liabilities buffer sustainable rather than a one-time stock.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The interaction separates firms whose liquidity is replenished by real economic earnings from those holding a static cash stock while consuming their asset base, a distinction invisible to either cash-flow or liquidity signals alone. Depreciation intensity also proxies for the reinvestment obligation that competes with debt service.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: ChronicLossShortRunway
EXPRESSION: MUL(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(pi), 0), 5), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(che, cogs))))
HYPOTHESIS: Repeated pretax losses only become terminal when the cash balance is small relative to the firm's operating cost base; the number of loss years over five years times the shortness of the cash runway (che scaled by cogs) identifies firms most likely to dilute or default, which underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Cash divided by cost of goods sold is an explicit runway concept that fuses the liquidity stock with the operating burn rate, and multiplying it by loss persistence rather than a single-year loss flag removes transitory-loss firms from the short leg. Firms with no loss years receive zero and stay neutral, so the spread comes from the chronically unprofitable tail.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
